title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-12-05
source: flac16/48kHz; Source: Sony F995 > Sony TC-124 > Cassette Master > DAT (48k) - Recorded by Harry Ely and provided by Tim Dalton; Tansfer: Dat > Panasonic SV-3700 > Tascam DA-3000 > wav 16/48 - Transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav 16/48 > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope Ozone 5 Advanced > CD Wave > TLH > Flac1648; edited and mastered SIRMick April 2018

ai_review.summary: Clean audience recording of a late‑'69 Dead show, delivering classic jams on The Other One, China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider and Dancin', with overall good sound quality for the era.
ai_review.review: The tape offers an unusually clear audience capture from December 1969 that sounds better than many early‑70s crowd recordings, though a taper can be heard singing during Cosmic Charlie. Musically the band provides a solid performance – The Other One sequence, China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, Uncle John > Main Ten and Dancin' stand out, while the shorter songs retain the period’s occasional looseness.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews consistently praise the show’s jams and note a surprisingly good audience recording; weighting shows (70%) and recording (30%) yields an overall rating in the low‑to‑mid‑four‑star range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Better clarity than most 1970 audience tapes, described as 'nice' and 'ultra clean'; minor background noise from a taper singing on Cosmic Charlie but otherwise clear.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid late‑'69 set with strong improvisational peaks and fun jams; the short songs show some of the era's typical looseness but overall the performance feels cohesive and enjoyable.

band_member_comments.Jerry: No specific guitar commentary, only a spoken remark is noted in the review.
